title: Little street bands versus the few good bands in town
summary: Charles says only four or five good bands existed: Robichaux, Superior, Imperial, Piron; Crescent played nothing but jazz.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well he played for the Buzzards for years, the Jefferson City Buzzards, every Mardi Gras. For a long time he had Archie Robinson and Booker T is the bass drum player, you know him, Henry Clash? And Dede Pierce, the trumpet player? That's right. You know Billy and Dede, do you know them? I don't know. No I knew Dede Butler. He used to play the accordion. Where's he from? New Orleans? New Orleans?
Who did he play with? Well that was the fellow that used to, you know the add-on when you didn't have nobody, you see?
You'd pick them up and play with you. Did they have a lot of little bands walking around the streets? Oh ask me how many. I can't, I'm afraid.
But you know I'm telling you we only had about five good bands, four good bands in the city.
That was Robichaud, the Superior that was Peter Bocard in there you see, Nile Parade that was the Imperial, and then they had Pierron.

Besides that the rest was, they were playing though, because you take the Crescent band, Frankie Duesen and them, Joe Ollivan they used to play. And people liked their music too because they played nothing but jazz, K-Roy, see? Nothing but jazz. Nothing but jazz. And then you know what I mean? I mean I'm afraid. I'm afraid. I'm afraid. I'm afraid. I'm afraid. But you know I'm afraid. I'm afraid. I'm afraid. I'm afraid. But you know I'm afraid. But dear
Oh yes. Oh yes. We played music there.
